content.question: How does SARSA update its Q-values, and what policy does this typically produce?
options: It updates based on the actual action chosen from the next state instead of the maximum over all possible actions, which often results in a more conservative policy that accounts for the cost of exploring when there might be risks.
It updates based on the maximum Q-value over all possible next actions, producing the most aggressive possible policy.
It updates Q-values only at the end of the session, producing no policy until then.
It replaces Q-values with confidence and lift scores, producing association rules instead of a policy.
content.answer: It updates based on the actual action chosen from the next state instead of the maximum over all possible actions, which often results in a more conservative policy that accounts for the cost of exploring when there might be risks.
